title: Rapid Credential Recovery & Evidence Automation Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines fast, auditable procedures for recovering access to critical credentials (credential recovery), performing emergency access when needed, and automating the collection and export of audit evidence into our SIEM. It ties together Vault management practices, RBAC v2 role mappings, audit log schema expectations, and evidence automation steps so an incident responder can act quickly with minimal lateral risk.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to secrets stored in HashiCorp Vault (primary), AWS Secrets Manager (secondary), and on-prem HSM-wrapped keys.
- Assumes RBAC v2 is enforced for all control-plane actions (no root interactive access for routine ops).
- Emergency access paths are exception-only and generate elevated telemetry for post-mortem.

High-level workflow (emergency credential recovery):
1) Triage & Authorization: The incident commander (IC) evaluates need for emergency credential access. If required, IC opens JIRA-SEC ticket and obtains approval from on-call SecOps lead. Approval must be recorded in the ticket and Slack incident channel.
2) Scoped Emergency Role: SecOps issues a time-limited, narrowly-scoped RBAC v2 grant called emergency_temp.<role>-<ticket> that allows only the specific vault path(s) and actions required. Grant TTL should default to 1 hour.
3) Vault Access & Extraction: Use vault CLI with MFA token bound to the temp role. All commands must be run with --audit-meta="ticket=JIRA-SEC-<id>" so audit records contain the incident id.
4) Evidence Automation: Trigger evidence capture job (see Evidence Automation section) which snapshots the following and forwards to SIEM/secure-archive: audit events, RBAC grant events, active sessions list, and extracted secret access logs.
5) Revoke & Rotate: Revoke temp grant immediately when done. If credentials were exposed, trigger automated rotation pipelines and record rotation evidence.
6) Post-incident Review: Attach all exported evidence to the ticket, run the post-incident checklist, and schedule an access policy review.

Emergency role creation (RBAC v2) - recommended policy bits:
- Purpose: create minimum-privilege role for a specific vault path for a bounded period.
- Example RBAC v2 binding (policy snippet - illustrative):
  kind: RoleGrant
  name: emergency-temp-storage-read-JIRA-SEC-4212
  subjects: ["secops:oncall:alice"]
  permissions: ["vault:read:/secret/production/payment-service/creds"]
  ttl: 1h
  audit_label: "incident=JIRA-SEC-4212"
(Actual grant API differs per control plane; use CLI alias rbac grant --subject ... --perm ... --ttl 1h --meta ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212)

Vault operations - safe pattern:
- Step 1: Create temporary grant (RBAC) for the exact secret path.
  Command example: vault rbac grant --subject "alice" --perm "read" --path "secret/data/prod/payment" --ttl 1h --meta "ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212"
- Step 2: Acquire session token bound to the grant and MFA.
- Step 3: Read secret with explicit audit metadata: vault kv get -format=json secret/data/prod/payment --audit-meta "ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212;step=extraction"
- Step 4: Log output only to ephemeral secure host; avoid pasting into Slack/Docs.

Rotation play (if secret exposed):
- Trigger the service-specific rotation job: infra/rotation/run-rotation --service payment-service --reason "incident JIRA-SEC-4212" --rotate-credentials --notify oncall
- Validate rotated key by running smoke tests on staging and then gradual rollout to prod; track with rollout-id in ticket.
- Record rotation artifacts: prereq-key-hash, post-rotation-config, smoke-test-logs.

Audit log schema (minimum fields our SIEM expects):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- event_id: UUID
- actor: "user:alice" | "service:rbac-controller"
- actor_id: internal id string
- action: e.g., "vault.kv.get", "rbac.grant.create", "rbac.grant.revoke", "kms.rotate"
- resource: canonical path (e.g., "secret/data/prod/payment")
- result: success | failure
- meta: semicolon-separated key=val (ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212;audit_label=incident=... )
- origin_ip: client IP or service id
- session_id: ephemeral session id used for correlation
- ttl: granted TTL for temp grants (if applicable)
Example audit event (log line - single-line JSON):
{"timestamp":"2025-02-10T16:22:33Z","event_id":"0f8fad5b-d9cb-469f-a165-70867728950e","actor":"user:alice","action":"vault.kv.get","resource":"secret/data/prod/payment","result":"success","meta":"ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212;step=extraction","origin_ip":"34.201.45.12","session_id":"s-3f2b8"}

Evidence automation (what to capture and how):
- Trigger: On creation of emergency role OR on manual request from IC.
- Capture bundle contents:
  1) All audit events for the ticket timeframe (timestamp ± 2 hours) filtered by meta.ticket.
  2) RBAC grant lifecycle events (create/rebind/revoke) with diffs.
  3) Active sessions list, with timestamps and last activity.
  4) Any commands executed on jump hosts (from shell history that is centrally collected).
  5) Rotations executed and verification logs.
- Automation path: secops-evidence-runner (k8s job) takes ticket id and queries control-plane APIs, packages artifacts, signs archive with KMS key, and posts metadata to SIEM endpoint and secure-archive S3.
- Output artifacts: signed-archive-url, evidence-manifest.json, siem-event-id.

SIEM export configuration notes (Elastic / Splunk):
- Use structured JSON events; avoid multiline logs. Include meta.ticket when present for easy searching.
- Splunk: forwarder config should map audit.event->index=sec_audit; add fields event_id, ticket, session_id.
- Elastic: ingest pipeline adds geoip for origin_ip and normalizes actor into actor.type and actor.id.
- Retention: audit events forwarded to SIEM are retained per compliance policy (90 days hot, 2 years cold for SOC audits).

Incident play examples (two quick scenarios):
A) Emergency read-only retrieval for database password:
  - IC authorizes. SecOps creates emergency-temp-read grant for exactly the DB secret path, TTL 30m. Evidence job auto-runs. Holder reads secret, rotates password within 15m, revokes grant, attaches evidence.
B) Compromised service account suspected:
  - IC authorizes full key rotation. Steps: revoke tokens for the account, create replacement keys via KMS rotation workflow, update confs via config-management with canary rollout, rotate dependent credentials, and collect evidence.

Post-incident checklist (must be completed before ticket closure):
- Evidence archive uploaded to secure-archive with signed link in ticket.
- All temp RBAC grants revoked and verified.
- Rotations completed and validated by smoke tests.
- Audit logs exported and SIEM events correlated (attach SIEM event ids).
- Root-cause note and policy/role changes proposed (if needed).

Operational tips and gotchas:
- Do not create broad wildcard grants under time pressure. If you must, escalate to Sec leadership and document rationale.
- Always include ticket id in audit metadata; it is the primary correlation key for automation.
- Ensure evidence-runner service account has only read access to audit stores and write access to secure-archive; separate privileges for signing key.

Appendix A — Quick CLI snippets:
- Create RBAC: rbacctl grant --subject alice --perm read --resource secret/data/prod/payment --ttl 1h --meta ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212
- Read secret: VAULT_TOKEN=... vault kv get -format=json secret/data/prod/payment --audit-meta "ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212;step=extraction"
- Revoke grant: rbacctl revoke --grant-id g-12345 --meta ticket=JIRA-SEC-4212
- Evidence runner: kubectl -n secops run job/evidence-collect --image=cli:latest -- args "--ticket JIRA-SEC-4212 --out s3://secure-archive/SE-4212"

Appendix B — Sample evidence manifest (fields our pipeline writes):
- manifest_id, ticket_id, collected_by, start_ts, end_ts, archive_url, signed_by, siem_event_ids.

Contact and escalation path:
- Primary SecOps on-call: pager: secops-oncall@redwood.ai (Slack: #secops-oncall)
- Security leadership: priya.kapoor@redwood.ai
- SRE (rotation assistance): eng-sre-oncall@redwood.ai

Notes and open questions:
- Consider integrating RBAC grant lifecycle webhooks directly to SIEM to reduce evidence collection lag.
- Evaluate adding ephemeral host-level session recording for jump hosts used in extraction.

Document history:

- 2024-12-12: Added audit schema and evidence-runner design (Marcus Chen).
- 2025-02-10: Clarified RBAC grant examples and SIEM mapping (Priya Kapoor).

End of playbook.
